title: Map GPU execution IDs to trace spans for attention/scheduler correlation
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Background:
We need deterministic correlation between what the serving scheduler decides (prefill vs decode path, batching/slicing decisions) and the exact GPU kernels that run so we can: 1) attribute tail latency to scheduling or kernel path choices, 2) surface attention-specific hotpaths in the Console, and 3) detect regressions introduced by kernel selection heuristics. Current telemetry emits NVTX ranges and trace spans, but mapping between scheduler events and per-kernel counters is noisy: kernel names are normalized inconsistently, NVTX ranges are coarse, and per-kernel metrics (from CUPTI/CUDA events) lack a stable execution identifier that ties them back to a single request or scheduler slice.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a short-lived, monotonic execution_id stamped at scheduler entry for each request slice. Propagate execution_id through: scheduler logs, NVTX push/pop payloads, and trace spans.
- Extend kernel attribution to include execution_id and a lightweight span tag (exec_type: prefill|decode, attention_path: fused|separate) so the collector can join kernel counters -> NVTX -> trace span -> request.
- Normalize kernel naming at runtime by emitting a canonical kernel_type tag (attention_fwd_v1, attention_fwd_v2, kv_cache_commit, dequant_gemm, softmax_fused) rather than raw symbol names.
- Use selective sampling: stamp execution_id for all requests but only attach verbose per-kernel counters for 1% of requests by default to keep overhead <2% latency budget. Non-sampled requests still have exec_id present for span-level attribution (duration, queue time).

Design details:
1) Runtime instrumentation changes:
   - Scheduler: generate a 64-bit hex execution_id at slice start and add to request context. Add light NVTX push with {exec_id, exec_type, seq_len_hint} before kernel submission.
   - Kernel wrapper: include a small header/annotation (NVTX range metadata) with canonical kernel_type and execution_id when available. Avoid string allocations on hot path: use integer enum codes and maintain a runtime mapping table for kernel_type -> short string emitted in telemetry client.
   - Collector: update trace ingestion to accept execution_id attribute and join kernel counters (CUPTI batches) by exec_id. Add aggregation layer to roll up per-exec kernel times into request-level breakdowns.

2) Telemetry schema changes:
   - New span attributes: execution_id, exec_type, kernel_type_code, attention_variant, scheduler_decision (batching|slice|standalone), queue_time_ms, submit_timestamp.
   - Per-kernel metrics: kernel_time_ms, sm_util_pct, l2_cache_misses, flops_estimate (optional), quant_mode.

3) Sampling & overhead controls:
   - Global sampling rate configurable via Console (default 1%).
   - When sampled, emit CUPTI-derived counters and expanded NVTX envelopes. When not sampled, emit only exec_id and coarse timing.
   - Microbenchmark: target <2% added p99 latency; initial spike shows ~1.1% overhead at 1% sampling on p4d-like hardware.

4) Dashboard & alerts:
   - New Console panels: per-exec waterfall (scheduler->nvtx->kernel), top kernel_type_code by average kernel_time_ms, attention_variant heatmap vs seq_len, and exec-level tail attribution.
   - Alerts: sudden increase in avg kernel_time_ms for attention_fwd_v2 or spikes in queue_time_ms tagged exec_type=decode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every request has stable execution_id available in tracing and logs.
- For sampled requests the dashboard shows per-kernel breakdown that can be correlated back to the scheduler decision within 2 minutes of ingestion.
- End-to-end overhead measured <2% p99 latency at default sampling on our staging clusters.
- PRs merged, documentation updated in Confluence, and Console panels created with example queries.

Implementation plan & milestones:
- Spike (done): prototype exec_id propagation in scheduler and NVTX envelope changes. Benchmarks: +0.9% overhead at 1% sampling. (see Confluence doc).
- Phase 1 (this sprint): kernel_type enum, execution_id propagation, basic collector join, trace attribute plumbing.
- Phase 2 (next sprint): CUPTI counters integration for sampled execs, dashboard panels, and rollout config.
- Phase 3: A/B rollout, perf regression automation (tie to CI perf tests), and SDK compatibility checks.

Open risks / blockers:
- CUPTI sampling introduces non-deterministic overhead on certain GPU drivers; need vendor-testing matrix.
- Kernel naming normalization must be comprehensive to avoid split attribution; requires small mapping file maintained in runtime.
- Some private deployments disable NVTX for policy reasons; fallback attribution path must rely on span timestamps and kernel_time heuristics.
